concept_name: The Underworld Life-Death Registry as Data Governance
definition: Data governance: access management, audit trails, and integrity guarantees for data. The Life-Death Registry exposed serious flaws in the underworld's data system
core_case: Wukong altering the Life-Death Registry, Kou Hong's life extension, and Li Shimin's return from the dead — these incidents exposed the access-control gaps and missing audits in the underworld's data system

data_incidents.incident_name: Sun Wukong wreaked havoc in the underworld · forcibly altered the Life-Death Registry
data_incidents.data_affected: The monkey-category Life-Death Registry · deleted his own name + the names of the monkey tribe
data_incidents.audit_trail: No · discovered by the underworld only after the fact
data_incidents.immediate_action: King Yama reported to the Jade Emperor · but Wukong had already escaped jurisdiction
data_incidents.long_term_action: No remedy · the Life-Death Registry was permanently altered
data_incidents.vulnerability: Access-control gap · the underworld had no physical defense
data_incidents.data_governance_failure: Total failure · core data was tampered with · no audit trail

data_incidents.incident_name: Li Shimin toured the underworld · returned from the dead and had his life extended
data_incidents.data_affected: Li Shimin's lifespan · changed from 13 years to 20 years
data_incidents.data_volume: 1 record · but involving the Son of Heaven
data_incidents.audit_trail: No · internal operation with no audit
data_incidents.immediate_action: Li Shimin returned from the dead · the underworld held no one accountable
data_incidents.long_term_action: No remedy · 'insider' operation left no trace
data_incidents.vulnerability: Excessive internal authority · the judge could alter lifespans at will

data_incidents.incident_name: Kou Hong's 13-year lifespan · underworld special approval for extension
data_incidents.data_affected: Kou Hong's lifespan · from death to resurrection + 12-year extension
data_incidents.immediate_action: Kou Hong returned from the dead
data_incidents.long_term_action: No remedy · but a 'lawful special approval'
data_incidents.vulnerability: High-level figures can freely grant 'special approval' · with no checks
data_incidents.data_governance_failure: Lawful but irregular · high-level authority has no checks

data_incidents.incident_name: Liu Quan delivered melons · returned from the dead to find his wife
data_incidents.perpetrator_identity: Highest in the Heavenly Court · Jade Emperor
data_incidents.data_affected: The lifespans of Li Cuilian + Liu Quan · both returned from the dead
data_incidents.audit_trail: Yes · signed by the Jade Emperor
data_incidents.immediate_action: Li Cuilian returned via a borrowed body + Liu Quan returned from the dead
data_incidents.long_term_action: No remedy · but a 'lawful special approval'
data_incidents.vulnerability: The highest level can freely grant 'special approval' · with no checks
data_incidents.data_governance_failure: Lawful but irregular · highest-level authority has no checks

data_incidents.incident_name: Wei Zheng beheaded the Jing River Dragon King · execution in a dream
data_incidents.perpetrator: Wei Zheng (human minister · Heavenly Court part-timer)
data_incidents.perpetrator_identity: Human minister · Heavenly Court execution supervisor
data_incidents.audit_trail: Yes · authorized by the Jade Emperor
data_incidents.vulnerability: None · but the 'human minister as Heavenly Court part-timer' mechanism is questionable
data_incidents.data_governance_failure: No failure · but the 'human minister as Heavenly Court part-timer' mechanism is questionable

data_incidents.incident_name: The Tongtian River Goldfish Spirit · ate boys and girls
data_incidents.incident_type: data staleness · the demon was not in the Life-Death Registry
data_incidents.data_affected: 18 lives of boys and girls · the Life-Death Registry had no record of the demon
data_incidents.data_volume: 18 records · but the demon was 'never registered'
data_incidents.audit_trail: No · the demon's descent went unrecorded
data_incidents.long_term_action: No remedy · the demon was 'never registered'
data_incidents.vulnerability: The mount's descent was not recorded in the Life-Death Registry · data-integrity failure
data_incidents.data_governance_failure: Data-integrity failure · the mount's descent was never registered

data_incidents.incident_name: The King of Wuji · returned from the dead after three years in a well
data_incidents.data_affected: The King of Wuji · returned from the dead after three years in a well
data_incidents.immediate_action: The king returned from the dead
data_incidents.long_term_action: No remedy · but a 'lawful special approval'
data_incidents.vulnerability: High-level figures can freely grant 'special approval' · with no checks

vulnerability_categories: Access-control gap (Wukong wreaked havoc in the underworld)
High-level special approval without checks (Ksitigarbha / Jade Emperor / Manjushri)
Data-integrity failure (mounts descending to earth never registered)

data_governance_insights: The Life-Death Registry exposed serious flaws in the underworld's data system
Of the 8 incidents, 1 was a total failure (Wukong's havoc) · 7 were lawful but irregular
Audit coverage is only 37.5% · 4 incidents have no audit trail
All compensation amounts are 0 · victims receive no compensation
Data-integrity failure: mounts descending to earth were not recorded in the Life-Death Registry
Chaotic access management: from grassroots (Wukong) to the highest level (Jade Emperor), anyone can alter the Life-Death Registry
The underworld's data governance is essentially 'rule by men' · not 'rule of law'
